before:
Police reports are required in Georgia in the following circumstances:
  • An injury or fatality resulted from the crash
  • There was property damage estimated at $500 or more
  • Your insurance company requires a police report
after:
Georgia law requires the driver to notify law enforcement of a crash immediately in the following circumstances (O.C.G.A. § 40-6-273):
  • An injury or fatality resulted from the crash
  • There was apparent property damage of $500 or more
Separately, your auto policy may require you to report the crash to your insurer, and many insurers ask for the police report when you make a claim. That is a policy condition, not a legal reporting duty.

before: Disputed errors are subjective statements or information that was recorded in the police report. These types of errors are probably the hardest to get removed. However, even if you cannot get them removed, you may be able to get them amended. These types of errors, especially, may be best handled with the assistance of a lawyer.
after: Disputed errors are the officer's conclusions, such as who was at fault or what contributed to the crash. These are the hardest to change, because only the investigating officer and agency can amend the report, and they will not rewrite a conclusion simply because a driver disagrees with it. These types of errors, especially, may be best handled with the assistance of a lawyer.

Mistakes in a police report could negatively affect your claim in many ways. Whether the information is wrong, left out or there are some other errors, it is important to get them corrected or amended as quickly as possible.

For instance, if you do not correct the fact about the other driver running the red light, you could get unfairly blamed for more than your share of fault. If that happens, it could impact how much you get compensated for your losses. This is because Georgia follows a modified comparative fault system.

before:
Depending on the type of error you find, there are several ways to get mistakes removed from your police report.

Get a Copy of Your Savannah Police Report

The first step is to request a copy of your police report right away. You can do this in person, by phone, by fax, snail mail or by email. The longer you wait to fix a report with errors on it, the more likely it is the officer who documented your report may not remember details about it.
after:
Depending on the type of error you find, there are several ways to seek a correction to your police report.

Get a Copy of Your Georgia Crash Report

The first step is to request a copy of your crash report right away. Statewide, the Georgia Department of Transportation (GDOT) is the custodian of Georgia crash reports; you can buy a copy through BuyCrash or mail GDOT's Individual Crash Report Request form ($5 per report, $2 more for a certified copy). Anyone named in the report, such as a driver, an injured person or their attorney, is entitled to it under O.C.G.A. § 50-18-72(a)(5). If Savannah Police investigated, you can also request a copy of your police report from its Records Unit in person, by phone, by fax, snail mail or by email; it may take up to three business days. The longer you wait to fix a report with errors on it, the more likely it is the officer who documented your report may not remember details about it.

before: Usually, providing documents with the correct details is enough to fix errors. If the license plate of your vehicle was documented incorrectly, for example, providing a copy of your current registration should be enough to get this changed.
after: For clerical errors, contacting the investigating officer with a document that shows the correct detail (your registration for a wrong plate number, your license for a misspelled name) is usually all it takes; the officer can then issue a corrected or supplemental report.

before:
• Contact the officer listed on the report and politely explain the error.
  • Ask if they can correct the statement.
  • If they will not change the statement, you can write your own account about the accident. Keep it concise and make sure it is clear and easy to read. Then sign, date it, and send it with a request to have your amendment attached to the original report.
  • When you write your statement, be sure that it is not just your opinion. Provide the facts without rambling – be clear, be brief and give details. If you have additional supporting evidence, like photos or dash cam footage, work with your attorney on the best way to send this amendment.

For a clerical error such as a wrong plate number or misspelled name, contact the investigating officer with a document that shows the correct detail. Only the investigating officer and agency can amend a Georgia crash report, and they will not rewrite a conclusion about fault simply because a driver disagrees with it. If the officer will not change it, write a concise, factual, signed and dated account and give it to your attorney. Fault errors cost money: under O.C.G.A. § 51-12-33 you recover nothing if you are 50 percent or more at fault, and your damages are reduced by any smaller share. Georgia law requires the driver to notify police immediately of a crash involving injury, death, or apparent property damage of $500 or more (O.C.G.A. § 40-6-273).
